settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: SecurityMemberAccess (lines 34-98) is the configured OGNL member access guard: it blocks static access unless allowStaticMethodAccess is set, excludes packages/classes, and applies accept/exclude property patterns, which constrains what an evaluated expression can do.
The error text path is reached only after a multipart parse failure; in normal uploads no exception message flows in.

Comments in LocalizedTextUtil for findDefaultText (lines 204-206, 236-238) state that neither the key nor the message is evaluated there, showing part of the API treats text as inert; the specific findText overload used here is the one documented as evaluating, so the behavior depends on the exact downstream implementation.
candidates.description: In JakartaMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage (lines 115-119), the error message key is built from the exception class simple name and the raw exception message is passed as the defaultMessage argument: `LocalizedTextUtil.findText(this.getClass(), errorKey, defaultLocale, e.getMessage(), args)`. The multipart parsing exception (org.apache.commons.fileupload) is triggered while parsing the attacker-supplied HTTP multipart request; its message can incorporate request-controlled data such as the Content-Type header, so e.getMessage() is untrusted input. LocalizedTextUtil.findText is documented (lines 345-380, and again 616-624) as evaluating the message text as OGNL expressions: "Both the key and the message itself is evaluated as required" and "Anything within ${...} will be treated as an OGNL expression and evaluated as such," using a ValueStack obtained from ActionContext (lines 391-394). Thus a parser exception whose message contains OGNL expression syntax such as ${...} could be interpreted as an OGNL expression during message resolution. The root cause is routing untrusted, request-derived text into a text-lookup API whose documented behavior includes OGNL evaluation against the ValueStack, rather than treating the default message as inert literal text. This is reported as a candidate; the exact code that evaluates the default message (getDefaultMessage) could not be read in this review, so end-to-end evaluation of e.getMessage() is unconfirmed. Note: whether findMessage for the constructed errorKey returns a bundle value first affects whether the default (raw message) path is even reached.
missing_evidence: The body of getDefaultMessage(key, locale, valueStack, args, defaultMessage) (referenced via search results but not readable in the allowed spans) that would show whether and how defaultMessage is passed to TextParseUtil.translateVariables / OGNL evaluation.
Whether findMessage for the generated 'struts.messages.upload.error.<ExceptionName>' key returns a bundle value, which would bypass the defaultMessage path.
The call site of JakartaMultiPartRequest.processRequest/parseRequest and how MultiPartRequestWrapper surfaces these errors to the response, to establish that the evaluated text is rendered/visited.
Whether commons-fileupload places arbitrary request header content into the exception message for the relevant exception types.
Confirmation that the configured ValueStack/OgnlUtil in this build evaluates ${...} default messages (runtime behavior, not visible statically).
preconditions: The request reaches the multipart file-upload handling path so that parsing is attempted and throws an exception (e.g. malformed/multipart Content-Type or a crafted multipart body).

The struts.messages.upload.error.<ExceptionSimpleName> key is not present in any resource bundle for the class/locale, so the resolution falls through to the defaultMessage (the raw exception message).
The exception message contains OGNL expression syntax (e.g. ${...}) that the text-resolution path would evaluate.
The LocalizedTextUtil.findText / getDefaultMessage path actually evaluates the default message with the ValueStack (this linkage was not fully readable in the reviewed spans).
candidates.title: Attacker-influenced multipart parser error message flows into LocalizedTextUtil (OGNL-evaluating text lookup)
